title: omr-ux findings
description: What every omr-ux pass returns, and what the merge script writes. finding-format.md is the human rendering of the same fields; skills/review/scripts/findings.py validates, merges, renders and compares files in this shape. Never type the report by hand.

skill.description: The pass that wrote this file, by its name in dispatch.md (laws, conformance, accessibility, ...), or the playbook for a merged file (calvin-sdlc:ux-review, calvin-sdlc:ux-audit).

version.description: Version of this contract the file was written against.

scope.description: What was looked at. A pass fills what it actually covered, not what it was asked to cover.

method.description: One line: how the evidence was gathered (running build, screenshots, code only) and whether the pass ran degraded.

degraded.description: Present only when the pass ran without its agent or skill: why, in one line. The report prints a banner for it.

passes.description: Written by the merge, one entry per pass file merged. A pass never writes it.

passed.description: Criterion or check ids that were checked and passed. Reports need these to tell 'clean' from 'not checked'.

not_applicable.description: Criterion or check ids that do not apply here, each with the applicability rule that excludes it.

did_not_run.description: Checks or whole passes that should have run and did not, each with the reason.

exceptions_used.description: Every recorded exception the pass relied on (conflicts.md section 2).

notes.description: Anything a person must decide, and anything the pass could not check. Not findings.

id.description: A stable rule or check id: L7.2, B5, WCAG-2.5.8, C3, IG-8, FTR-3, H4, DOC-glossary.

lens.description: The standard the id belongs to: laws, wcag, heuristics, lenses, writing, conformance, responsive, e2e-coverage, sitemap, documents, spec.

impact.description: The five levels of finding-format.md, the kit's only scale.

rung.description: The rung of conflicts.md that the finding breaks; the impact follows it.

conflict.description: Only when a conflict was settled: the rung that won over the one that lost, and the exception. Example: R4 (IG-8) over R5 (L7.4), EX-3.

location.description: Somewhere a person can open: file:line, or route + state + width (/leads empty 390), or a selector on a named route. Two findings are the same only when id and location match exactly.

summary.description: The problem in plain language, the finding's title. No codes.

current.description: Current experience: a concrete example, the exact words on screen.

recommendation.description: The change, and how it helps the user's workflow.

tradeoff.description: The main downside; an alternative only when meaningfully different.

decision_needed.description: One plain question, or 'Routine fix: no individual decision needed'.

verified.description: seen on screen, read in the code, measured, assumption (not checked), owner's preference.

evidence.description: Screenshot paths, file:line references, measured values with their unit.

component.description: The shared part the defect lives in, so one defect repeated across pages reads as one cause.

owner_words.description: The earlier request quoted with its date, or 'no earlier request found'.

supporting_notes.description: Further supporting-note lines of finding-format.md, each with its label: 'Earlier IDs: F012', 'Other products: Linear opens a side panel', 'Guideline: IG-8'.

sources.description: Which passes reported it. A pass may leave it out; the merge always writes it.

allOf.description: Evidence is real: seen, code and measured name what proves them.
R1, the legal floor, is Critical.
R7, taste, is never above Design choice.
